Landed as Gerrit change 3110 (commit 431d5c6b76b, LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, 0 unresolved). The diff touches only tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py; no production code changed.

Loosened bound, documented: the _ref_backend fixture now sets _ref_lock._LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS to 60 s for each test (monkeypatch restores it), with a docstring saying why. The production bound stays 5.0 s and a timeout still means HELD (fail-closed). The tests assert lock semantics, not latency.

Evidence, 2026-10-25 09:21-09:22 PDT, on the merged tree:
1. pytest tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py -q -> '7 passed in 19.02s'. This includes test_ref_backend_roundtrip_survives_a_slow_local_git_call, whose PATH shim sleeps 5.6 s before 'git update-ref'.
2. Same test against a temporary copy of the module with the fixture's 60 s override line deleted -> fails with subprocess.TimeoutExpired on 'git ... update-ref', the path that reports 'timed out after 5.0s'. The copy was deleted afterwards.
3. pytest tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_ref_lock.py -q -> '18 passed in 9.12s'; test_timeout_raises_reflocktimeout is unchanged and still pins the fail-closed behavior.
Earlier delayed-shim runs: update-ref delayed 1 s and 4.5 s pass; 5.6 s fails on the old fixture.

Unverified: the original slow update-ref (on a host running 4 concurrent suites) has no recorded cause. The fix removes the dependence on a 5.0 s wall-clock bound in tests; it does not explain that slow call.

Reviewer advisory (non-blocking, not acted on): the slow-git test does not assert that its shim actually ran, so it could pass without exercising the delay if the PATH shim stopped being used. Item 2 shows the delay does take effect today. A new patchset would have restarted CI and the full verify for a test-only assertion.
